title: Let a method that throws IOException fit a Function

blocks.text: `Function<T, R>` declares no checked exceptions, so a reference to a method that `throws IOException` does not compile as a `Function`. The page's fixes are a custom functional interface that declares the exception, and a wrapper that catches it.
`IoFunction<T, R>` is given: its `apply` may throw `IOException`. Write two methods in `Unchecked`:

items: `<T, R> Function<T, R> function(IoFunction<T, R> fn)` returns a `Function` that calls `fn`. An `IOException` is rethrown as an `UncheckedIOException` carrying it as the cause.
`<T, R> List<R> mapAll(List<T> items, IoFunction<T, R> fn)` applies `fn` to every item, in order.

blocks.text: With `static String load(String key) throws IOException` in scope, both of these compile and work:
Wrap only what the standard interface cannot carry; anything else the method throws should reach the caller as it was thrown.

cases.says: A reference to a method that declares IOException works through the wrapper, one value or a whole list.
An IOException comes out as an UncheckedIOException whose cause is the original exception.
A runtime exception from the method comes out as itself, not wrapped.
The UncheckedIOException carries the very exception the method threw as its cause, not a new IOException copying its message.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: A method that throws a checked exception fits only an interface that declares it, so for the standard interfaces it is wrapped.
